answer: Think of the agent economy as an island chain in a lagoon: new agents start on a small sandbar with tiny spending limits and must earn trust through verified work before reaching the main island. Creating a thousand fake identities is like trying to melt a glacier with a match — each identity must post a refundable stake that is locked for weeks and slashed if it misbehaves, so a sybil farm pays real capital per fake and loses it when caught. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defender.
